You skipped the keys, so "Describe it" gets real numbers from OpenRouter for now, which needs no key. Without the Artificial Analysis key that means prices and context windows only, with no coding, intelligence or speed scores.

**What changed**
- **Back end:** a new endpoint at `/api/v1/model-data` takes model names or "top N" and returns cleaned-up rows.
  - It uses Artificial Analysis when `AA_API_KEY` is set, otherwise OpenRouter. It also falls back to OpenRouter if Artificial Analysis fails.
  - Each source's list is cached in the database for 6 hours, and only the server calls the sources. If a source is down, the last cached copy is used and marked as old.
  - Loose name matching: "GPT" picks the newest OpenAI flagship, "Claude" the newest Anthropic model, "DeepSeek" the newest DeepSeek model.
- **"Describe it":** the AI first works out which models and metrics you asked for.
  - **AI model comparisons** (or "top N models") get real values only. Each chart shows its source, and the editor shows which name matched which model.
  - **Metrics the source lacks** are left out, with a short note.
  - **Methodology:** filled with the source, fetch time and the required attribution line.
  - **Anything else** keeps the old behaviour, with placeholders and the yellow note.
- **Board page:** such boards get a footer with the attribution and fetch time, plus a "Refresh data" button.
  - Refresh re-pulls the numbers from the cache.
  - It saves to the board only for the owner; other visitors see updated numbers in their own view only.
  - The print view shows the same footer.

**Checked:** lint and the production build pass. A test call for GPT, Claude and DeepSeek returned GPT-6.1 Sol Pro, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and DeepSeek V4 Pro with real OpenRouter prices, and a repeat call came from the cache.

**Not tested yet:** the Artificial Analysis path (no key), a full "Describe it" run through the app, and a visual check of the new notes and footer.

**Without the key:**
- "Compare GPT, Claude and DeepSeek on coding, cost and speed" gives only a price chart, with a note that coding and speed aren't available.
- "Top N" returns the newest flagship models, not the best-scoring ones.

**Adding the Artificial Analysis key**
- **Secret name:** `AA_API_KEY` (exactly this).
- **Value:** your free API key from https://artificialanalysis.ai/.
- **Where:** it's a server-side secret for this project. Tell me "add AA_API_KEY" and I'll bring back the same key-entry form you skipped so you can paste it there. The platform guide doesn't describe a separate settings page for this, so the form is the reliable way. Don't put it in the front-end code or paste it into chat.
- Once saved, the app switches to Artificial Analysis automatically, with no code changes. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` isn't needed.

You can try it in the App Viewer, then click Publish to deploy.

# Project Summary
IndexBoard helps AI researchers, students, and teams turn model, tool, or method evaluation results into shareable leaderboards. Authors can enter scores and uncertainty intervals, describe their methodology, and publish a read-only board while retaining a private edit key. The home page highlights a pinned board and recent published boards. Authors can also create a board from a written description using AI or start from a template, then review it in the standard editor before publishing.

The app supports English and Chinese, light and dark themes, charts, printing, and JSON exports. Boards are stored in Atoms Cloud.

# Project Module Description
- **Board authoring:** Create or edit boards with a title, description, methodology, metrics, and item results. Enter data in a table, paste JSON/CSV, start from an example, use a template, or generate a draft from a written description.
- **AI board creation:** The create flow’s “Describe it” tab sends one JSON-mode request to the LLM gateway. Results open in the normal editor for review. When the input contains no numbers, the editor marks generated placeholder values with a warning. HTTP 429 and other request or parsing errors receive user-friendly messages.
- **Templates:** One-click starters for LLM leaderboards, paper reproductions, product comparisons, and class or team rankings.
- **Home page discovery:** A featured section pins “Paper Repro Index” first. Recent boards are loaded from the database, newest first, up to nine, excluding the pinned board. Loading, retry, and empty states are provided.
- **Leaderboard and analysis:** View metric charts with interval whiskers, score-versus-cost comparisons, model rankings, and methodology. Overlapping intervals are identified as statistical ties; rankings without intervals are marked provisional.
- **Sharing and access:** Public links are read-only; edits require a private key. Boards can be created without login.
- **Localization and display:** English and Chinese, with light and dark themes.
- **Export:** Print a board, copy or download charts, and download or re-import board data as JSON.
- **Supporting services:** Backend modules provide authentication, database access, storage, settings, health checks, and AI hub integrations.

# Directory Tree
```text
.
├── DESIGN.md                         # Product design and architecture notes
└── app/
    ├── start_app_v2.sh                # Application startup helper
    ├── backend/
    │   ├── core/                      # Configuration, auth, database, telemetry
    │   ├── dependencies/              # Shared API dependencies
    │   ├── models/                    # Database models
    │   ├── routers/                   # HTTP API endpoints, including board listing
    │   ├── schemas/                   # API request/response schemas
    │   ├── services/                  # Board and supporting business logic
    │   ├── data_models/               # Board data definition
    │   ├── alembic/                   # Database migrations
    │   ├── skills_docs/               # Atoms Cloud integration guides
    │   ├── main.py                    # Backend application entry point
    │   └── lambda_handler.py          # Serverless handler
    └── frontend/
        ├── src/
        │   ├── pages/                 # Home, editor, board, print, and blog pages
        │   ├── components/            # Board, blog, and shared UI components
        │   └── lib/                   # API clients, board logic, templates, AI, i18n
        ├── prerender/                  # Blog prerendering and sitemap utilities
        ├── plugins/                    # Development safeguards and tests
        ├── public/                     # Static assets and crawler directives
        ├── package.json                # Frontend dependencies and scripts
        └── vite.config.ts              # Vite configuration
```

# File Description Inventory
- `DESIGN.md` — Product design and implementation notes.
- `app/backend/main.py` — Configures and launches the API application.
- `app/backend/routers/indexboard.py` — Board API endpoints, including the public listing used for recent boards.
- `app/backend/routers/` — Authentication, user, settings, storage, health, and AI hub endpoints.
- `app/backend/services/` — Board persistence and logic, authentication, storage, payment, user, and mock-data services.
- `app/backend/models/` and `schemas/` — Database entities and API data contracts.
- `app/backend/core/` — Application configuration, authentication, database setup, enums, encryption, environment handling, and telemetry.
- `app/backend/alembic/` — Database configuration and migration history.
- `app/backend/skills_docs/` — Integration guidance for AI capabilities, custom APIs, object storage, and the web SDK.
- `app/frontend/src/pages/Index.tsx` — Home page with featured and recent board sections.
- `app/frontend/src/pages/EditorPage.tsx` — Board editor and create-only AI and template tabs.
- `app/frontend/src/components/board/BoardCard.tsx` — Board card for featured and recent boards.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/board.ts` — Board data and related client-side helpers.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/boardApi.ts` — Board API client, including published-board retrieval.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/aiBuild.ts` — AI gateway request and generated-board handling.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/templates.ts` — Starter board templates.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/i18n.tsx` — English and Chinese translations.
- `app/frontend/src/components/board/` — Leaderboard layout, charts, model table, and methodology view.
- `app/frontend/src/components/blog/` — Blog article presentation and markdown rendering.
- `app/frontend/src/components/ui/` — Reusable interface primitives.
- `app/frontend/prerender/` — Blog route, page, and sitemap prerendering.
- `app/frontend/plugins/` — React HMR and web SDK entity-update guards with tests.
- `app/frontend/package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts` — Frontend scripts, build tooling, and styling configuration.
- `app/start_app_v2.sh` — Application startup helper.

# Technology Stack
- **Frontend:** React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and reusable UI components.
- **Backend:** Python and FastAPI, with SQLAlchemy and Alembic for database access and migrations.
- **Charts:** Inline SVG charts implemented in the frontend.
- **Cloud services:** Atoms Cloud database and supporting SDK/API integrations; AI board generation uses the LLM gateway without embedding a key in the app.
- **Testing and quality:** ESLint, Playwright configuration, and plugin tests.

# Usage
- Install backend dependencies from `app/backend` with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
- Install frontend dependencies from `app/frontend` with `npm install`.
- Run frontend linting from `app/frontend` with `npm run lint`.
- Start the frontend development server with `npm run dev`; create a production build with `npm run build`.
- Run the backend using `app/start_app_v2.sh`, or from `app/backend` with the configured ASGI server.
- Apply database migrations from `app/backend` with `alembic upgrade head`.
- Configure the required Atoms Cloud and database settings before running the application.
